page: Amazon Web Services r6i.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C) clocked at 3.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this bare-metal host provides 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled, delivering direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead. It incorporates hardware virtualization support via VMX, advanced vector processing through AVX-512 extensions with VNNI, and robust hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

Memory density is a primary architectural feature of the r6i.metal, offering 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional memory throughput, recording 338.62 GB/sec for large uncached read operations and over 6.6 TB/sec for cached read bandwidth. Synthetic CPU benchmarks reflect top-tier multithreaded capacity, with a PassMark CPU score of 87,484.14 and strong parallel performance across Geekbench compilation and stress-ng tests.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 50 Gbps, accommodating heavy outbound and inter-node data exchange. A key architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local instance storage, requiring all persistent and scratch volumes to rely on network-attached Amazon EBS. Additionally, the instance contains no discrete GPU hardware, limiting its applicability for accelerator-dependent machine learning training pipelines.

Given its massive memory footprint, extensive core parallelism, and direct hardware control, the r6i.metal is suited for in-memory databases such as Redis, large-scale enterprise SAP workloads, distributed big data processing frameworks, memory-intensive ETL pipelines, and high-density container virtualization clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services r6i.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, it achieves an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside exceptional memory throughput and top-tier multithreaded processing metrics. The bare-metal configuration eliminates hypervisor virtualization penalties while offering AVX-512 extensions and dedicated 50 Gbps baseline networking. Because the host lacks local disk storage and GPU accelerators, storage operations rely exclusively on external network-attached volumes. This resource distribution makes the platform well aligned with memory-bound enterprise systems, massive in-memory caching engines like Redis, high-throughput database deployments, and large-scale parallel processing jobs.
